I could not find a next cardboard collection date for 8004 in the indexed sources.

Postcode 8004 resolved to Zurich District 4 (Kreis 4). The tools report no documents indexed for District 4 itself, so evidence came only from the parent jurisdictions of the City of Zurich, the Canton of Zurich, and federal law. None of the returned documents contains a collection calendar with dates. Two searches, one with the waste category hint and a 25-result limit, returned only general pages and no calendar entries with an event date.

The closest source is the City of Zurich waste disposal overview page, which links to the city's disposal calendar tool ("Entsorgungskalender: When and where is my waste collected?"): https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/umwelt-und-energie/entsorgung.html. That calendar itself is not indexed, so I cannot quote a date from it.

To get the actual date, enter your street address in the city's disposal calendar on that page or in the Sauber Zürich app. If you want, I can add the Zurich disposal calendar to the ingestion sources so this question can be answered from indexed data in future.

I could not find an answer in the indexed sources. Seefeld resolves to a neighborhood in Zurich's District 8, but the tools report no local data for either Seefeld or District 8. The searches then fell back to city, canton, and federal documents, and none of those cover leash rules or off-leash zones.

What the indexed sources do and do not contain:

- **Seefeld and District 8** have zero indexed documents. Any answer would have to come from parent jurisdictions.
- **City of Zurich pages** returned were only navigation overviews for mobility, cycling, walking, traffic safety, and nature. None mentions dogs, leash obligations, or dog exercise areas. Examples: https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/umwelt-und-energie/natur.html and https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/mobilitaet/zu-fuss.html
- **Canton of Zurich pages** returned were the environment and animals landing page and agriculture statistics, again with nothing on dog leash rules: https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere.html
- **Federal law** hits were the Animal Welfare Act (SR 455), the Road Traffic Act (SR 741.01), and the Forest Act (SR 921.0). None of these sets leash or off-leash rules for dogs. Those are cantonal and municipal matters in Switzerland.

So the honest answer is that the swiss-grounding index currently has no evidence on where dogs may run off leash in Seefeld or anywhere in Zurich. The relevant rules would be the Canton of Zurich dog law and the City of Zurich's dog regulations and dog exercise zone information, but neither is indexed yet. This fits the project note that ingestion is frozen and expansion to more Swiss sources is planned.

records.answer:
The indexed sources don't answer this. None of the documents indexed for Zürich city, Canton Zürich, or federal law mention a dog leash requirement in forests, in July or in any other month.

What I checked:

- **Zürich city** has 17 indexed documents and **Canton Zürich** has 12, but three searches (English and German, with the dogs category) returned nothing about leash rules. The location "Zürich" was resolved to the municipality. The canton alone gave the same result.
- **The canton's forest page** (https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html) only says the forest is freely accessible to everyone by law and links to fact sheets such as "Merkblatt 2 – Besucher im Wald". The fact sheet itself is not indexed.
- **Federal law hits** were the Forest Act (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1992/2521_2521_2521/20250801/de) and the Animal Welfare Act (https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/2008/414/20230901/de). Neither snippet sets a leash rule.
- **Schweizer Wanderwege's summer hiking page** (https://www.schweizer-wanderwege.ch/de/wandern/unterwegs/wandern-im-sommer) only advises keeping dogs away from areas with livestock guardian dogs.

So I can't confirm from these sources whether a July leash obligation applies in Zürich forests. In Canton Zürich the relevant rule sits in the cantonal dog and hunting legislation, which is not in the index. The forest division's contact is on the canton page above (wald@bd.zh.ch) if you want an authoritative answer.

Gleichzeitig dient er der Erholung der Bevölkerung und bietet Raum für Bildung und Ausbildung. Alle Leistungen werden sorgfältig aufeinander abgestimmt, um den Wald langfristig zu erhalten und an den Klimawandel anzupassen.**\\n\\n## Auf dieser Seite\\n\\n* Zahlen und Fakten\\n* Waldpionier\\n* Kontakt\\n\\n## AKTUELL\\n\\n* Feuerverbot im Wald und in Waldesnähe - Medienmitteilung vom 26.6.2026\\n* Waldbrandgefahr\\n* Der Eichenprozessionsspinner - Hintergrundwissen und Handlungsempfehlungen\\n\\n## Zahlen und Fakten zum Zürcher Wald\\n\\n### Wussten Sie, dass …\\n\\n… fast ein Drittel der Zürcher Kantonsfläche bewaldet ist?\\n  \\n… nicht nur die Bergkantone, sondern auch der Kanton Zürich Schutzwälder hat?\\n  \\n… der Wald gemäss Gesetz allen Personen frei zugänglich ist?\\n  \\n… unsere Wälder das sauberste Trinkwasser liefern?\\n  \\n… der Kanton Zürich der drittgrösste Holzproduzent der Schweiz ist?\\n\\nWeitere Informationen und Zahlen zum Zürcher Wald finden Sie in unserer kleinen Broschüre:\\n\\n* Download\\n\\n  Züriwald - Wer bisch du?\\n  PDF | 16 Seiten | Deutsch | 5 MB\\n\\n## Elias Landolt\\n\\n### Oberforstmeister und Professor (1821 - 1896)\\n\\nElias Landolt war von 1864 bis 1882 Oberforstmeister des Kantons Zürich und Professor für Forstwissenschaft an der ETH Zürich von 1855, dem ETH-Gründungsjahr, bis 1893. Sein Leben fiel in eine Epoche, die wie keine andere zuvor von wissenschaftlichen Durchbrüchen gekennzeichnet war. Untrennbar damit verbunden war die Industrialisierung mit ihren drastischen Folgen für das Leben und die Umwelt. Landolt war der wohl bedeutendste Schweizer Forstmann. Auf ihn geht der noch heute geltende Schutz des Schweizer Waldes zurück.\\n\\nZum Andenken an ihn hat die kantonale Abteilung Wald zusammen mit dem Verband Zürcher Forstpersonal VZF und dem Verband der Waldeigentümer WaldZürich ein Büchlein erstellt.\\n\\n* Download\\n\\n  Zum 200. I could not find the dog tax amount for the City of Zürich in the indexed sources.

The location resolved correctly to the City of Zürich, and the index does hold documents for the city, the canton, and the Confederation. Two searches, one in English and one in German with the dogs category, returned only unrelated pages: a cantonal agriculture page, city pages on nature and walking, and federal animal welfare and environment law. None of them states a dog tax figure.

Pages the tools returned, none of which answer the question:
- https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/landwirtschaft.html (canton agriculture and livestock statistics)
- https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/umwelt-und-energie/natur.html (city nature overview)
- https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/2008/414/20230901/de (federal Animal Welfare Act, SR 455)

The city's dog tax page is not in the index, so I cannot give an amount with a citation. The authoritative source would be the City of Zürich's dog registration page under stadt-zuerich.ch, which is where the current annual rate is published.

The indexed Swiss sources do not say who maintains hiking trail signposts in Zürich. I ran two searches scoped to Zürich and pulled the one signpost-specific document in full. None of the returned material assigns maintenance responsibility.

What the sources do cover:

- **Schweizer Wanderwege** explains how to read a signpost and the trail categories (yellow, white-red-white, white-blue-white) but not who installs or maintains them. https://www.schweizer-wanderwege.ch/de/wissen/signalisation/der-wegweiser-erklaert
- **Schweizer Wanderwege** notes Switzerland has around 65,000 km of signposted trails, again without naming a maintainer. https://www.schweizer-wanderwege.ch/de/wandern
- **Canton of Zürich** environment pages surfaced only because they are tagged "hiking". They discuss environmental enforcement and the "Wegweiser Bau & Umwelt" municipal guide, which is a document guide, not a trail signpost. https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/umweltschutz.html
- **Federal law** hits (nature protection SR 451, forest law SR 921.0, road traffic SR 741.01) are unrelated to trail signage.

Coverage note: the location resolved to the municipality of Zürich rather than the canton. Both jurisdictions have documents indexed, but the federal Footpaths and Hiking Trails Act and any Zürcher Wanderwege material are not in the index, so the answer cannot be grounded here.

I can't give you a grounded answer for Winterthur. The swiss-grounding index has no documents for Winterthur itself, and the evidence it returned from the parent jurisdictions does not address leash rules.

What the tools cover:

| Jurisdiction | Indexed documents |
|---|---|
| Switzerland | 18 |
| Canton of Zurich | 12 |
| Winterthur | 0 |

What the returned sources actually say:

- **Federal Forest Act (SR 921.0)** covers motor vehicles on forest roads and tree-felling permits, not dogs. https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1992/2521_2521_2521/20250801/de
- **Federal Animal Welfare Act (SR 455)** sets general duties of care for animal keepers and says nothing about leashes in forests. https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/2008/414/20230901/de
- **Canton of Zurich forest page** lists fact sheets on waste, forest work, liability and fire bans. No leash rule appears in the indexed text. https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html
- **Canton of Zurich environment and animals page** points to dog-owner information but the indexed content has no leash provisions. https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere.html

Leash obligations in Zurich forests are set by the cantonal dog law and hunting regulations, plus municipal police rules, and neither is in the index. The canton's dog information page linked above is the right place to check, along with the City of Winterthur's own website.

"Wil" is ambiguous. There are two municipalities with that name, Wil in canton St. Gallen and Wil in canton Zurich, and the tools hold no local documents for either one. Neither the St. Gallen cantonal level nor either municipality has any indexed data, so I cannot give you a binding local leash rule.

What the sources do say:

- **Swiss Hiking Trails guidance** advises keeping dogs on a leash, especially in the forest, and respecting wildlife rest zones and protection areas. This is a recommendation from a hiking association, not a law. Source: https://www.schweizer-wanderwege.ch/de/wandern/unterwegs/like-to-hike
- **Federal forest law** (SR 921.0) contains no dog leash rule in the retrieved passages. Source: https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1992/2521_2521_2521/20250801/de
- **If you mean Wil ZH**, the Zurich canton forest page was returned, but the retrieved excerpt lists fact sheets on waste, forest work and events, not dog rules. Source: https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html

In Switzerland, leash obligations in forests are set by cantons and communes, often as a spring leash period during wildlife breeding season. Those rules are not in the indexed data for either Wil, so check the municipal website or the cantonal hunting and forest office for the Wil you mean. Tell me which canton and I can search again, though coverage will still be limited to the sources above.

What the sources do say:

- **Federal forest law** (SR 921.0, Art. 14) requires cantons to keep forests open to the public but lets them restrict access where wildlife or plant protection requires it. This is the legal basis for cantonal or municipal leash rules, but it does not set one itself. https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1992/2521_2521_2521/20250801/de
- **Canton Zurich's forest page** covers fire bans, waste, and forest work, but the indexed chunks contain nothing on dogs or leashing. https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html
- **Canton Zurich's environment and animals page** points dog owners to the "Animals" topic area but again has no leash content in the index. https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere.html

The canton's dog law and Dietikon's own police regulations, which are where a forest leash rule would normally live, are not indexed. To get a reliable answer, check Dietikon's municipal police ordinance or contact the Stadtverwaltung Dietikon directly. I can also search for the cantonal Hundegesetz if you want me to try other wording.

The indexed sources do not contain a leash rule for Zürich Oberland forests, so I cannot confirm one from them.

What the tools returned:

- **Location resolution.** "Zürich Oberland" is a region, not a commune. The tool did not recognise it below canton level and answered at the level of the Canton of Zurich. The canton has 12 indexed documents and Switzerland has 18. No local data exists for any Oberland municipality.
- **Cantonal forest page.** The Canton of Zurich forest page states that the forest is freely accessible to everyone by law and links a fact sheet on forest visitors, but the indexed text says nothing about dogs or leashes. Source: https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html
- **Federal forest law.** The Federal Act on Forest covers access, clearing and vehicle use, not dog leashing. Source: https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1992/2521_2521_2521/20250801/de
- **Federal animal welfare law.** The Animal Welfare Act sets general care duties and penalties but contains no leash rule. Source: https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/2008/414/20230901/de

Leash rules for dogs in the forest are set by the cantonal hunting and dog legislation and by individual municipalities. Neither is in the index, so the definitive answer has to come from the canton's hunting authority or your municipality. The cantonal forest page lists the Office for Landscape and Nature, Forest Division, as the contact at +41 43 259 27 50 or wald@bd.zh.ch. If you tell me which Oberland municipality you mean, I can check whether it has local data.

The indexed sources don't contain a specific leash rule for the forest at Zurich Airport.

**What the tools cover.** "Zurich Airport" was not recognised below canton level, so the search answered at the level of the canton of Zurich. Neither the airport area nor the municipality of Kloten has its own local data indexed. The canton has 12 indexed documents and the federal level 18, but none of them states a forest leash obligation.

**What the sources do say:**

- Schweizer Wanderwege, the national hiking association, advises keeping dogs on a leash, especially in the forest, and respecting wildlife rest zones. This is guidance, not law, and is framed around the winter season. Source: https://www.schweizer-wanderwege.ch/de/wandern/unterwegs/like-to-hike
- The canton of Zurich forest page confirms that forests are freely accessible to everyone by law and links a fact sheet on "Visitors in the forest", but the indexed page text contains no dog-leash rule. Source: https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html
- The federal Forest Act only appears with general provisions on forest area and clearing, nothing on dogs. Source: https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1992/2521_2521_2521/20250801/de

**Bottom line.** Based on the indexed data I cannot confirm whether a legal leash obligation applies in the forest near Zurich Airport. The cantonal dog law and any Kloten municipal rules are not in the index. The closest grounded advice is the hiking association's recommendation to leash dogs in the forest. For a definitive answer, the cantonal Forest Division listed on the zh.ch page above is the contact point.

The indexed Zürich sources do not contain the specific cardboard page. Here is what they do give you.

**The City of Zürich's waste disposal portal is the right entry point.** Its landing page lists a disposal calendar ("Entsorgungskalender", when and where your waste is collected), a "where and when to dispose" section with disposal locations, and a "what to dispose of" section that covers waste categories and their options. Cardboard would be covered by those subpages, but the tool has only indexed the overview page, not the cardboard-specific details, so I cannot confirm collection days or drop-off sites from the tool data.

Source: https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/umwelt-und-energie/entsorgung.html

**Notes on the data:**
- The location "Zürich" was resolved to the municipality of Zürich. It could also mean the canton of Zürich.
- Coverage: 17 documents for the city, 12 for the canton, 18 federal. None of the returned chunks mention cardboard directly.
- The federal Environmental Protection Act (SR 814.01, Art. 31b) confirms that municipal waste disposal is the cantons' and municipalities' responsibility, which is why the city portal is the authoritative place to look: https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1984/1122_1122_1122/20260801/de

To get the exact cardboard collection dates for your address, use the disposal calendar linked from the city page above.

**Next paper collection in 8003 (Zurich District 3): Tuesday, 29 September 2026.**

After that it runs roughly every two weeks, on Tuesdays:
- Tue 13 October 2026 — [source](https://openerz.metaodi.ch/api/calendar?region=zurich&zip=8003&sort=date&limit=100#paper-2026-10-13)
- Tue 27 October 2026 — [source](https://openerz.metaodi.ch/api/calendar?region=zurich&zip=8003&sort=date&limit=100#paper-2026-10-27)

I couldn't find an answer for this one.

**Seefeld has no local data.** The tools resolve Seefeld (`CH-ZH-261-K8-SEEFELD`), but report **0 documents indexed for Seefeld and 0 for District 8** — evidence only comes from the parent jurisdictions (City of Zurich: 17 docs, Canton Zurich: 12, federal: 18).

And in those parent jurisdictions, nothing covers off-leash areas. Searching under the "Dogs and pets" category for Zurich returned only:

- Generic City of Zurich landing pages — nature/[stadt-zuerich.ch/de/umwelt-und-energie/natur.html](https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/umwelt-und-energie/natur.html), mobility/[on foot](https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/mobilitaet/zu-fuss.html) — none of which mention leash rules
- Canton Zurich's [environment & animals overview](https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere.html), which points dog owners to permits and dog-incident reporting, but says nothing about where dogs may run free
- Federal law on animal welfare ([SR 455](https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/2008/414/20230901/de)) and road traffic ([SR 741.01, Art. 50](https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1959/679_705_685/20260701/de)) — about animal transport, keeping bans, and leading animals along roads, not off-leash zones
- [Schweizer Wanderwege on summer hiking](https://www.schweizer-wanderwege.ch/de/wandern/unterwegs/wandern-im-sommer), which only advises against bringing dogs into areas with livestock guardian dogs

I tried to flag the City of Zurich dog page as a source to index, but stadt-zuerich.ch is already a registered source — the specific dog/Hundeauslaufgebiete pages just aren't in the index yet. So the gap is coverage depth, not a missing source.

One caveat on what is indexed: both the Canton Zurich (zh.ch) and Schweizer Wanderwege feeds report `degraded` health, with failures in their last ingest run.

I searched the Swiss grounding index for Zürich (it resolved to **Zurich municipality**, `CH-ZH-261`; note the tool flagged that "Zürich" could also mean the canton). **The indexed sources do not contain a dog-leashing rule for forests — I can't answer your question from them.**

What coverage exists, so you know this isn't a "no data for this place" case:
- Zurich municipality: 17 documents (Stadt Zürich, 15, health ok; zh.ch and Schweizer Wanderwege, 1 each, degraded)
- Canton Zurich: 12 documents (zh.ch, degraded)
- Switzerland: 18 documents

So there is local data — it just doesn't cover dog leash obligations. The closest things the searches returned:

- **Forest Act, SR 921.0 Art. 14** — cantons must keep forests publicly accessible, but must restrict access to specific forest areas where protection of plants and wild animals requires it. This is the legal hook under which a seasonal leash or access rule would sit, but the indexed text doesn't state any such rule for Zurich. https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1992/2521_2521_2521/20250801/de
- **Animal Welfare Act, SR 455 Art. 6** — general duty to care for and supervise animals you keep; no leash provision. https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/2008/414/20230901/de
- **Canton Zurich, environment and animals** — notes that breaches of animal-welfare/environmental rules are enforced by municipal authorities with fines. https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere.html
- **Canton Zurich forest page** (fact sheets, current forest notices such as fire bans) — nothing on dogs. https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html
- **Stadt Zürich, nature / city forest** — topic overview only, no leash text in the index. https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/umwelt-und-energie/natur.html
- **Schweizer Wanderwege, hiking in summer** — advises not bringing dogs into areas with livestock guardian dogs; not a forest leash rule. https://www.schweizer-wanderwege.ch/de/wandern/unterwegs/wandern-im-sommer

The two sources most likely to carry the actual rule (cantonal hunting/dog legislation on zh.ch, and the Stadt Zürich dog pages) are either not indexed or only partly indexed, and both zh.ch rows show degraded fetch health. I'd check the canton's dog/hunting law pages directly, or ask Kreisforstamt / the city's Hundewesen office, before relying on an answer here. This is retrieved public information, not legal advice.

## Short answer: the indexed sources don't answer this

"Zürich" resolved to **Zurich, the municipality (CH-ZH-261)** — it could also have meant the canton (CH-ZH). Both were searched, since the tool includes all parent jurisdictions.

Zürich is *not* an uncovered location — there are 17 documents indexed at municipality level, 12 at cantonal level, 18 federal. But **none of them states who is responsible for erecting or maintaining hiking trail signposts.** I'd rather tell you that than guess at an answer the evidence doesn't support.

### What the indexed sources do cover

Schweizer Wanderwege has signage pages in the index, but only the descriptive parts:

- **[Signalisation](https://www.schweizer-wanderwege.ch/de/wissen/signalisation)** — the overview page explicitly promises to explain "who actually takes care of making sure these [signposts] are placed throughout the landscape," but the indexed text stops at the teaser; the sub-page that answers it isn't in the corpus. It also links a *Handbuch Signalisation* "for those responsible for hiking trails" (Für Wanderwegverantwortliche), which isn't indexed either.
- **[Der Wegweiser erklärt](https://www.schweizer-wanderwege.ch/de/wissen/signalisation/der-wegweiser-erklaert)** — how to *read* a signpost: location and elevation, destinations, hiking time, trail category (yellow = Wanderweg, white-red-white = Bergwanderweg, white-blue-white = Alpinwanderweg), route stickers, and intermediate markers. Nothing on who maintains them.

On the legal side, the Federal Act on Footpaths and Hiking Trails (SR 704) — the law that actually assigns this duty — is **not** among the five indexed federal acts (SR 451 nature/landscape, SR 455 animal welfare, SR 741.01 road traffic, SR 814.01 environment, SR 921.0 forest). The nearest hits were about road signage and forest management, neither of which governs hiking signposts.

Cantonal (zh.ch) and city (stadt-zuerich.ch) results were all general navigation pages — [environment](https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere.html), [mobility](https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/mobilitaet.html), [on foot](https://www.stadt-zuerich.ch/de/mobilitaet/zu-fuss.html) (urban pedestrian traffic, not hiking trails). No trail-maintenance page is indexed.

### One caveat on data health

Three coverage rows are flagged **degraded** (last ingest run had failures): `schweizer_wanderwege` at both CH and CH-ZH-261 level, and `zh.ch` at both cantonal and municipal level. So the gap may be partly an ingestion failure rather than a true absence at the source.

### Already flagged

A source suggestion for **`https://www.zuercher-wanderwege.ch`** is already pending in the system (submitted 2026-09-16), proposed for extent CH-ZH under the `hiking` category, with the note that it is the cantonal hiking trail association that signposts and inspects the network on the canton's mandate and takes reports of damaged signposts. That's a proposal awaiting review, not indexed evidence — I can't cite it as an answer, only report that the gap is known and queued.

I can't answer this one from the indexed sources — here's exactly what they do and don't have.

## No local data for Winterthur

Winterthur resolves cleanly as a municipality (`CH-ZH-230`), but coverage is **0 documents at the municipal level**. Evidence only exists for the parent jurisdictions: 12 documents for the Canton of Zurich and 18 federal. The tool flags this itself: *"No documents indexed for Winterthur; evidence comes from parent jurisdictions."*

## The parent-jurisdiction sources don't contain a leash rule either

I searched the federal and cantonal layers four ways (leash duty, dogs and wildlife, Zurich dog regulations, forest conduct rules). Nothing in the indexed corpus states whether dogs must be leashed in the forest. What it does contain, adjacent to your question:

- **Forest Act, SR 921.0 Art. 14 (Accessibility)** — cantons must keep the forest accessible to the public, and *must* restrict accessibility for specific forest areas where preserving the forest or other public interests, "in particular the protection of plants and wild animals," so require. This is the legal hook under which leash duties and seasonal area restrictions get imposed, but the article itself imposes no leash obligation: https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1992/2521_2521_2521/20250801/de
- **Canton of Zurich forest page** — general forest information and fact sheets (forest waste, events in the forest, fire risk); no dog or leash rule in the indexed text: https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html
- **Canton of Zurich environment & animals page** — confirms the canton holds information on dog incidents and that *municipal* authorities handle enforcement, which points at exactly the Winterthur-level document that isn't indexed: https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere.html
- **Swiss Hiking Trails** — the only leash guidance in the corpus is about pastures, not forests: keep dogs on a short leash and give cows a wide berth (https://www.schweizer-wanderwege.ch/de/wandern/unterwegs/like-to-hike), and avoid areas with livestock guardian dogs altogether (https://www.schweizer-wanderwege.ch/de/wandern/unterwegs/wandern-im-sommer)

Two caveats on the evidence quality: both the `zh_ch` and `schweizer_wanderwege` sources report **degraded** health, so their last ingest runs had partial failures.

## What I did about the gap

I filed a source suggestion for `https://stadt.winterthur.ch` (suggestion #2, pending human review), scoped to `CH-ZH-230` under the dogs/safety categories — leash duties and local leash zones in Zurich are set municipally, so that's where the real answer lives.

Practically: since federal law leaves this to cantonal and municipal rules, and the one enforcing level has no coverage here, treat this as unanswered rather than as "no leash needed." The City of Winterthur's dog regulations or Stadtpolizei Winterthur would be the authority to check directly.

## Short answer

I can't give you a binding answer for Wil from the indexed sources — **neither Wil has any local data**.

**First, the ambiguity:** "Wil" resolves to two municipalities, and the tools flagged it as ambiguous rather than picking one:
- **Wil ZH** (`CH-ZH-71`), Canton Zurich
- **Wil SG** (`CH-SG-3427`), Canton St. Gallen

I ran the question against both. Coverage came back:

| Jurisdiction | Documents indexed |
|---|---|
| Switzerland | 18 |
| Canton Zurich | 12 |
| Canton St. Gallen | **0** |
| Wil (ZH) | **0** |
| Wil (SG) | **0** |

Both searches returned `resolution_note: "No documents indexed for ... ; evidence comes from parent jurisdictions."`

## What the available evidence does and doesn't say

**No leash rule exists in the indexed material.** The federal acts that came back — the Forest Act ([SR 921.0](https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1992/2521_2521_2521/20250801/de)), the Animal Welfare Act ([SR 455](https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/2008/414/20230901/de)), the Nature and Cultural Heritage Act ([SR 451](https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1966/1637_1694_1679/20250801/de)) and the Road Traffic Act ([SR 741.01](https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1959/679_705_685/20260701/de)) — cover forest clearing permits, animal husbandry and transport, species protection and livestock on roads. None of them imposes a leash duty in the forest. The Canton Zurich forest and environment pages ([zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html](https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html), [zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere.html](https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere.html)) likewise carry no leash rule in what's indexed.

**The one on-point hit is advice, not law.** Schweizer Wanderwege's "Like to Hike" page says to *"stay on marked trails, keep dogs on a leash, especially in the forest, and respect wildlife rest zones or wildlife protection areas"* — but that appears in a **winter-hiking** section, and it's institutional guidance from a hiking association, not a binding rule for your commune.
→ https://www.schweizer-wanderwege.ch/de/wandern/unterwegs/like-to-hike

## What this means for you

Leash duties in Switzerland are typically set at cantonal and **municipal** level (seasonal leash requirements during breeding season, local leash zones), and that's exactly the layer where the index has nothing for either Wil. So I can't confirm whether a leash is required, and I'd rather say that than infer a rule.

To get a real answer, check your commune's dog regulations directly — **stadtwil.ch** for Wil SG, or **wil-zh.ch** for Wil ZH — or ask the municipal office. If you tell me which Wil you're in, I can note the gap as a source suggestion so it's covered next time.

## Short answer

I can't confirm this from the indexed sources — **Affoltern am Albis has 0 documents indexed** at municipal level. Everything below comes from its parent jurisdictions (Canton of Zurich: 12 documents, Switzerland: 18), and none of it contains a forest leash rule.

## What the indexed sources do say

**Forests are open to the public by default, but the canton can close areas to protect wildlife.** Forest Act Art. 14 (SR 921.0): the cantons must keep the forest accessible to the general public, and where preservation of the forest or other public interests — "in particular the protection of plants and wild animals" — require it, they must restrict accessibility for specific forest areas.
https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1992/2521_2521_2521/20250801/de

That is the legal hook under which wildlife rest zones and seasonal leash zones get created, but the indexed material does not tell me whether any such zone covers Affoltern am Albis forest.

**The Animal Welfare Act does not impose a leash duty.** SR 455 Art. 6 covers keeping animals appropriately, including the "freedom of movement necessary for their well-being" — an owner duty, not a leash rule.
https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/2008/414/20230901/de

**The cantonal pages for animals and forest carry no leash rule** in what's indexed — they are topic landing pages (permits, animal welfare enforcement, forest fire bans, forest fact sheets).
https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere.html
https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html

## The gap

In the Canton of Zurich, leash duties and local leash zones are set by **municipal** dog regulations (Hundeverordnung) — and that is precisely the level with no coverage here. The same gap was already recorded for Winterthur, with a pending source suggestion to fix it.

So: I can't tell you yes or no. Check the Affoltern am Albis municipal dog regulations directly, and watch for on-site signage marking wildlife rest zones (Wildruhezonen), where a leash duty typically applies seasonally.

I can file a source suggestion for the Affoltern am Albis municipal site so this question is answerable next time — say the word.

I can't answer this one from the indexed sources — here's exactly what the lookup found.

**Dietikon has no local data.** The location resolves to `CH-ZH-243` (municipality, Canton Zurich), but the index holds **0 documents for Dietikon itself**. Everything below comes from parent jurisdictions (Zurich: 12 docs, Switzerland: 18 docs), and the cantonal source `zh_ch` is currently flagged `degraded`.

**No leash rule appears anywhere in the indexed federal or cantonal material.** Searching for it (both in English and for "Leinenpflicht / Hundegesetz / Wildruhezeit") returns only adjacent law, none of which imposes a leash duty:

- **Forest Act, SR 921.0 Art. 14** — the cantons must keep the forest publicly accessible, but *may restrict accessibility for specific forest areas* where conservation or "the protection of plants and wild animals" requires it. That's the legal hook a leash zone would hang on, but it doesn't itself create one. https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1992/2521_2521_2521/20250801/de
- **Animal Welfare Act, SR 455 Art. 4 / Art. 6** — general duties of care toward your own animal, nothing about control in public. https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/2008/414/20230901/de
- **zh.ch forest page** — cantonal forest information (fire bans, forest functions); no dog or leash content. https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html

**What this means practically:** in the Canton of Zurich, leash duties and local leash zones are set by *municipal* dog regulations and by seasonal wildlife-protection signage — neither of which is indexed for Dietikon. So I can't tell you whether Dietikon's forest has a year-round leash requirement, a spring wildlife season (typically April–July in many ZH communes), or none at all. Don't read the absence of a rule here as permission to let the dog run free; check the City of Dietikon's own dog regulations and any signage at the forest entrance.

Note the index already has a pending suggestion for exactly this gap in a neighbouring commune (Winterthur, filed today for the identical question). Want me to file one for `stadt.dietikon.ch` too, so this is answerable next time?

## Short answer: the indexed sources don't contain a leash rule for your location.

**Location:** "Zürich Oberland" is not a jurisdiction the grounding index recognises. It resolved only approximately, at **canton Zurich (CH-ZH)** — the tool's own note: *"'Zürich Oberland' was not recognised below canton level; answered at Zurich (canton)."* So there is **no local data for Zürich Oberland itself**; coverage exists only at canton level (12 documents, source `zh.ch`) and federal level (18 documents).

### What the sources do say

**Forest access is a federal baseline, not a dog rule.** Forest Act (SR 921.0) Art. 14 "Zugänglichkeit":

> The cantons shall ensure that the forest is accessible to the general public. Where the preservation of the forest or other public interests, such as in particular the protection of plants and wild animals, so require, the cantons shall: a. restrict accessibility for specific forest areas […]
> — https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/1992/2521_2521_2521/20250801/de (Art. 14, in force 2025-08-01)

That is the hook under which access restrictions — including leash zones — get imposed, but the article itself imposes none.

**The cantonal pages don't carry a leash rule either.** The Zurich forest page (https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere/wald.html) and the environment-and-animals page (https://www.zh.ch/de/umwelt-tiere.html) cover fire bans, forest events, liability and animal welfare, but no leash obligation. The animals page does note that enforcement of animal-welfare and environmental rules is a municipal task, and that breaches carry fines or imprisonment.

**Nothing in the Animal Welfare Act (SR 455) either** — Art. 4 and Art. 6 set general duties of care and freedom of movement, not leash requirements: https://www.fedlex.admin.ch/eli/cc/2008/414/20230901/de

### What this means for you

I can't tell you whether you must leash your dog in your forest, because the rule that would answer it isn't in the index. Leash duties and seasonal leash zones in canton Zurich are set at the **municipal** level, and no Zürcher Oberland commune (Wetzikon, Uster, Hinwil, Rüti, Pfäffikon, Wald …) has any documents indexed.

Tell me which commune you walk in and I'll re-run the search against it — though based on current coverage it will likely come back empty too, in which case that commune's own dog regulation (*Hundeverordnung* / *Polizeiverordnung*) is where to look, plus any posted signage at the forest edge, which is how seasonal wildlife-protection leash zones are normally communicated.

Two caveats on the data itself: the `zh.ch` source is flagged **degraded** (2 fetch failures in the last ingest run on 2026-09-14), so cantonal coverage may be incomplete. And per the tool: retrieved public information from Swiss sources, not legal advice.

**I can't give you a definitive answer for Zurich Airport — the indexed sources contain no leash rule that applies there.**

Two gaps, both worth knowing:

**1. The location doesn't resolve below canton level.** "Zurich Airport" was matched only to the *Canton* of Zurich (`geoadmin_approximate`), with the note: *"'Zurich Airport' was not recognised below canton level; answered at Zurich (canton)."* Searching the underlying municipality directly — Kloten — resolves cleanly but returns: *"No documents indexed for Kloten; evidence comes from parent jurisdictions."* Kloten has **0 indexed documents**. Coverage is 18 documents federal, 12 cantonal, 0 municipal.

**2. No leash obligation exists in the federal or cantonal material that is indexed.** Searching under the `dogs` and `hiking` categories surfaced the Forest Act, the Animal Welfare Act, the Nature Protection Act and the cantonal forest pages — none of them impose a leash duty. That matters because in the Canton of Zurich the leash rule is normally set at municipal level, which is exactly the layer with no coverage here.

What the indexed sources *do* say:
